app.title: Pediatric Status Asthmaticus Ventilation Simulator
app.summary: The person picks a built-in scenario and adjusts its patient, airway mechanics, ventilator and therapy settings in a sidebar. Each change re-runs a deterministic simulation. The person reads headline maxima and minima, risk badges and automatic teaching points, then looks at time-series curves grouped by pressures, gas exchange, haemodynamics and mechanics. They can pick a second scenario as a comparator, read a per-metric delta table marked better or worse, and see overlaid curves. At the end they download the comparison delta or the full simulated time series as CSV, and can view the exact scenario configuration that was run.

task.text: Run a mechanistic model under settings the person chooses and see how the settings trade off against each other over time, against a comparator strategy.

data.text: Scenario configurations (patient, mechanics, ventilator and therapy parameters) are turned into simulated physiological time series, plus summary metrics and risk labels per run.
data.item: one simulated scenario run: a time series of pressures, gas-exchange and haemodynamic quantities over the simulation's duration

stage.text: exploring ventilator strategy trade-offs in a teaching model, by setting strategies against each other

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls rewrite a copy of the base scenario, and every change re-runs the simulation, which redraws the metric tiles, teaching points and tabbed line charts. A comparison tab simulates a second scenario on the same duration and time step, then shows a delta table and overlaid curves that can be exported.

field.text: lumped-parameter respiratory mechanics simulation for teaching mechanical ventilation in critical care medicine

workflow.name: tune a model's inputs, run it, and compare the outcome against a reference run

steps.here: A 'Base scenario' selector loads one of the built-in YAML scenarios.

Sidebar sliders, selects and checkboxes set duration, time step, patient, airway resistance and compliance, ventilator mode, rate, PEEP, I:E ratio and therapies. The tidal-volume, pressure-control and pressure-support fields appear only for the modes that use them.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Every change re-runs the simulation. Eight metric tiles show max auto-PEEP, max plateau, final PaCO₂, min MAP, min pH, the VEI proxy and the barotrauma and haemodynamic risk badges. Threshold rules turn these into teaching points.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Tabs switch between line charts over time for pressures, gas exchange, haemodynamics and mechanics.
A comparator scenario is simulated on the primary run's duration and time step. A delta table labels each metric better, worse or context-dependent, and primary and comparator curves are overlaid.
Download buttons save the comparison delta CSV or the full time-series CSV. An expander shows the exact scenario YAML that was simulated.

distinctive: Which input fields appear depends on the ventilation mode: tidal volume, pressure control or pressure support.
The comparator run is forced onto the primary run's duration and time step so the overlaid curves line up.
Each compared metric carries a fixed direction (lower is better, higher is better, or context-dependent), so a delta is read as better or worse.
Fixed teaching thresholds on plateau pressure, hyperinflation volume, MAP, pH and the EtCO₂–PaCO₂ gap generate plain-language warnings.
The exact simulated configuration is shown back as YAML for reproducibility, and every output is labelled an educational surrogate, not a prediction.
